speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, Minister Josephine Teo, Minister of State Desmond Tan and I will address a total of 39 Parliamentary Questions (PQs) that have been posed to MAS, MCI and MHA arising from the recent OCBC phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They cover a wide range of issues – from whether the banks can do more to mitigate the risks of such scams, to how the telco infrastructure, enforcement actions and consumer education can be enhanced to deal with this growing problem.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The breadth of the issues raised underscores that we need to take an ecosystem approach to strengthen our collective defence against phishing scams and scams in general.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Everyone in this ecosystem must play their part.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Ministerial Statements will explain the Government’s comprehensive approach, working with each party in the ecosystem, to counter the threat of phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will provide more details on the OCBC phishing scam and on the steps that MAS and the banks are taking to strengthen safeguards against such scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister Josephine Teo will then set out the measures being taken to enhance the broader communications infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And Minister of State Desmond Tan will elaborate on measures to strengthen enforcement and consumer education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: None of these measures can be foolproof in and of themselves, but, collectively, they should work to significantly reduce the scope for scams to succeed and their cost.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With everyone on guard, including individuals, the industry and infrastructure providers, we hope not to see a recurrence of a large-scale scam as was seen in the OCBC case.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Taken together, Minister Josephine Teo, Minister of State Desmond Tan and I will address Oral Question Nos 7 to 32 and Written Question Nos 1, 2 and 8 on yesterday’s Order Paper, Oral Question Nos 1 to 5 and Written Question Nos 1, 2, 9 and 27 on today’s Order Paper.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman has filed an Oral Question scheduled for a future Sitting on these issues.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As today’s Ministerial Statements will address these questions, Mr Speaker, I would like to invite these Members to seek clarifications should they have any on these issues after the Statements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Spoofed SMSes were sent with a fake sender ID, which, in many cases, made them appear in the same message thread as genuine SMSes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The victims, having received the spoofed SMSes in the same thread of messages from OCBC, were deceived into clicking the links in these SMSes that led them to scam websites.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These scam websites were almost indistinguishable from the real OCBC website, such that people could not tell the difference unless they compared the URL of the scam website with that of the genuine one.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hence, many keyed their login credentials and one-time passwords (OTPs) into the scam websites.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The scammers used these credentials and OTPs to take control of the victims’ bank accounts and made fraudulent transfers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I should add that this was not a cyber attack on OCBC but a phishing scam on OCBC’s customers who were deceived into providing their banking credentials and OTPs at scam websites set up by the scammers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At no time was the bank’s own systems breached.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In its efforts to stem the phishing scam, OCBC took various actions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It warned customers to be alert to spoofed SMSes, initially through general advisories on its website, and then, subsequently, through SMSes and emails to customers; it worked with the Singapore Police Force and the Cyber Security Agency to block and take down the scam websites; it ceased sending customers SMSes with clickable links; it enhanced its anti-scam controls; and it verified through a phone call every customer who submitted a request for digital token activation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These actions were taken at various stages during the month as the phishing scams built up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: OCBC should, however, have responded faster and more robustly at the first sign of the scams, which the bank had picked up in early December.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: OCBC informed MAS on 24 December that it had activated its incident response team.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By then, the OCBC call centre was overwhelmed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It faced a surge in calls from affected customers as well as other worried customers who had not themselves received phishing messages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite the bank deploying additional resources, some affected customers experienced delays in reaching the bank to report the scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To address Dr Tan Wu Meng’s query, prior to the OCBC incident, MAS had received only a few complaints concerning delays in customer service related to similar scams, in other words, the spoofed SMSes that impersonated banks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: OCBC has apologised for falling short of its own expectations in customer service and response.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has made arrangements to do so with all the affected customers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: OCBC has also engaged an independent external party to conduct a thorough review of its anti-scam processes, including fraud surveillance, incident management and customer service, and to recommend necessary remedial actions, on top of what it has already done.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS will review these findings, take appropriate supervisory actions against the bank and closely monitor the bank’s implementation of remedial measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has long had in place expectations for banks to have measures to secure the risk of digital banking.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, banks have to implement multi-factor authentication, such as dynamic passwords or OTPs that can only be used once, to verify the customer’s identity and to authorise online transactions; they must maintain fraud monitoring systems to facilitate timely detection and blocking of suspicious transactions; and they must send notification alerts to customers for outgoing transactions, including credit card transactions, that exceed a threshold that customers can determine, so that they can report unauthorised transactions as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: SPF, MAS and banks have also been issuing regular advisories to alert the public to online scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister of State Desmond Tan will touch on that later.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In view of the increase in the number of scam cases, particularly in the last two years, MAS had, in the third quarter of last year, carried out a focused supervisory review of the adequacy of fraud controls in the digital banking channels of the three local banks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In October 2021, MAS conveyed to each of the banks its specific findings and recommendations for the remediation of the gaps observed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In agreeing to the timelines for implementation, MAS was mindful that the banks had multiple priorities, including mitigating the overarching cybersecurity threat that has been rising and ensuring business continuity and robust risk management, amidst COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When faced with the escalation in phishing scams in December 2021, OCBC fast-tracked the implementation of some of the measures identified in MAS’ supervisory review.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, it extended the cooling period after a digital token is set up on a new mobile device, during which, higher risk transactions cannot be carried out.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The recent OCBC scam signifies a step-up in the persistence and deceptiveness of phishing scams involving banks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The scammers used a combination of well-orchestrated tactics, to achieve a level of realism not seen in previous phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government is, therefore, further strengthening the safeguards in digital banking channels and the broader ecosystem to help thwart this enhanced threat.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has accelerated the process of strengthening anti-scam control standards across all retail banks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These measures will substantially bolster the security of digital banking against scammers employing similar tactics as the OCBC scam cases.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These measures have reduced the risk of successful phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond these immediate measures, banks can and should do more to safeguard their customers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS and ABS have stepped up work on further measures to comprehensively strengthen banks’ ability to deter, detect and combat phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members have also raised some useful suggestions on additional measures that can be put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, banks are working to further strengthen their fraud surveillance capabilities to identify suspicious and anomalous transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most banks do have some rule-based parameters to trigger suspicion, for example, large transfers to a new recipient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But these parameters need to be expanded to take account of a broader range of scam scenarios.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such algorithms should be based on multiple sources of information, including customer profile and vulnerabilities, past transaction patterns, account activity and mobile device identification.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I must caveat that while these advances will help, fraud monitoring systems are not a silver bullet.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not possible to detect every scam.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, banks should step up their ability to immediately block suspicious transactions and reach out to their customers to verify their authenticity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The transactions will be unblocked and processed only upon confirmation by the customer.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Banks today do have some of these capabilities, but they are not consistent across various types of transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also looking into enabling customers to trigger a freeze on their own accounts without having to contact the banks if they suspect their accounts have been compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will introduce some friction to customers carrying out genuine transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will all need to adapt and get used to these inconveniences, in order to strengthen the security of digital banking.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fourth, banks are exploring expanding the use of biometric technology, in addition to passwords and OTPs, as a means of authentication.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will add one more layer of security that cannot be easily phished by scammers to access a customer’s account.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fifth, banks will accelerate the shift towards the use of mobile banking apps for customer authentication, transaction authorisation and delivery of bank notifications.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If implemented well, it will be harder for scammers to abuse mobile banking apps.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, MAS and the banks are reviewing the use of SMS to deliver OTPs and the potential measures that should be taken to reduce risk if such a practice should continue.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The techniques employed by scammers are constantly evolving and gaining in sophistication.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why in the fight against scams, banks need to employ a combination of measures in prevention, detection, response and recovery, and constantly review and recalibrate these measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of our banks already have many of these measures in place in one form or another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS will work with the banks to strengthen these measures and set minimum parameters.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it would be counter-productive to publish the specific calibration of these controls.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is no different from why the red flags that banks look out for to detect money laundering transactions are not published in full.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The enhanced measures that banks are taking will mitigate the risks posed by phishing scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But realistically, it will not be possible to eliminate such scams completely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has set out expectations for banks to treat their customers fairly when looking into reports of fraudulent transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These include comprehensively investigating all cases and suspending late fees for disputed card transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond this, it is important to establish a common and equitable framework for sharing the losses incurred by the customer.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: No matter which bank you go to, you should still receive the same fair treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: OCBC’s recent goodwill payouts to fully cover customer losses were made as a one-off gesture and do not set a general precedent for future cases.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under this framework, both banks and their customers have their respective responsibilities and the share of losses each party bears will depend on whether and how the party has fallen short of its responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Financial institutions should bear an appropriate share of losses arising from scams, but care must also be taken to ensure that any compensation paid to customers does not weaken their incentive to be vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Other than financial institutions, the players operating the communications infrastructure play a key role in digital security against scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, MCI and MAS will consider the shared responsibilities of all the key parties in the ecosystem to ensure that there is proper accountability.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To conclude, Sir, let me assure Members that digital banking itself is safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The threat we are facing is one of deception of customers, where scammers mimic bona fide communications and transactions to gain the trust of victims, induce in them a heightened state of anxiety or excitement, and exploit their lapse of attention to steal their credentials and passwords.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the same way that we are all vulnerable to misinformation, we are also vulnerable to scams and must not be complacent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The digital world we live in today demands a posture of constant vigilance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional measures put in place by banks will mean more controls that a scammer will have to overcome, but they cannot guarantee that a customer will not be deceived.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: SPF and MoneySense, the national financial education programme, will continue to step up their public education efforts to provide useful tools and tips that can help members of the public avoid falling prey to scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is no dominant customer profile of scam victims across different scam types, whether by education, wealth, age or gender.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The problem of scams requires robust responses at the individual, industry and infrastructure levels – in short, an ecosystem approach where the various measures work in synergistic fashion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are addressing the risks at every part of the digital ecosystem, so that, taken together, the measures will significantly mitigate risks for the entire system and enable us to operate safely in a digital world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I had explained earlier, this must involve the financial sector but it must go beyond it.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has been working in close coordination with MHA and MCI on a Government-wide approach towards scams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, Minister Josephine Teo and Minister of State Desmond Tan will elaborate on this in their Statements.
